lines.text: One agent, five projects, and one big pile of tasks. Things start to leak into each other.
The agent has to guess which project a task belongs to. Sooner or later it guesses wrong, and edits the wrong repo.
And you cannot see the state of any one project, because the board is a jumble of everything at once.
Agent R Q gives each project its own workspace. A clean room, with only that project in it.
Each workspace has its own tasks, its own history, and its own live event stream.
Each workspace also has its own M C P token, so an agent only sees the project it belongs to.
Pick a different agent for each project. Claude on the storefront, Codex on billing, Gemini on the docs.
Each workspace has its own memory and skills, shared by its agents, and invisible to the other projects.
When an agent needs you, that one workspace lights up, so you know exactly where to look.
Settings follow the workspace too. Auto approve in the docs site, and stay strict in billing.
A new project means a new workspace. Ten projects do not feel messier than two.
Every project, in its own room. Try workspaces at Agent R Q dot com.
